transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I almost didn’t come in, because I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. But lately there have been mornings where I wake up and think… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up at all.

I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I just… that thought scared me enough that I thought I should talk to someone. Is that okay to say?
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?
About a month, I think. It started after my sister died unexpectedly… I don’t mean that every single minute has been like that, but that’s when those thoughts began showing up. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities that you normally enjoy?

A little, yes… I mean, I still go to things. I don’t want to just disappear on people, so I make myself go to book club, and there’s a dance night I’ve kept showing up for.

But lately it’s like I’m there and not really there, if that makes sense. Like I’m behind a pane of glass watching everyone else enjoy it. Even being in my garden, or cooking something for the neighbors, which usually gives me a little lift… it just doesn’t feel the same right now. I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you experienced a significant loss of energy or fatigue since your sister passed away?

Yes… I suppose I have, though I keep telling myself it’s just normal, you know, after everything.

But even small things have been taking it out of me. Running a simple errand, or getting papers together for the Cultural Center… things I used to do without thinking… I’ll finish and feel completely worn out, like I’m moving through thick mud. I don’t know if that counts as significant, but it does feel different.
Have you been feeling consistently sad or empty most of the day since your sister passed away?

I’m not sure I’d say consistently, no… I mean, of course I’ve been sad, but “most of the day” sounds so definite. I do have stretches where I’m just sort of quiet or hollow, but then I’ll distract myself or be around people and it’s not as noticeable. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your sister passed away?

A little, I think… I haven’t been trying to lose weight or anything. It’s more that food just doesn’t seem to call to me the way it used to.

I’ll make myself something small, like toast or a bit of soup, and then later in the evening I’ll realize I barely ate much at all. I don’t know how much my weight has changed exactly, but my appetite is definitely off, if that’s helpful.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness and emptiness for most days over the past two weeks?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been there most days.

It’s been about a month now, really — since my sister died so unexpectedly. Some days are better than others, but those sad, empty feelings have been coming up pretty regularly. Is that what you mean?
Have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up nearly every day?

Nearly every day… yes, I think so. I don’t want to worry anyone, and I’m not planning to hurt myself or anything like that.

But what scared me enough to ask for help is that I keep having mornings where I think it might just be easier if I didn’t wake up. That sounds terrible to say out loud… but that’s what it’s been like.
For how many months have you been feeling this way since your sister passed away?
About a month, I’d say… since my sister died so unexpectedly. It feels like maybe I should be handling it better by now, but that’s when it started.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find pleasure in at all?

A little, yes… though I’m still trying to keep up with things. I still go to book club, and sometimes the dance night, because I don’t want to just sit at home.

But lately I’m there and it feels like I’m sort of behind a pane of glass, if that makes sense. Even my garden, or cooking something for the neighbors — things that used to give me a nice little lift — they just don’t seem to do that the same way right now. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but now find you don't enjoy at all?

Not completely “at all,” maybe… I mean, I do still make myself go to book club and sometimes the dance night, because I don’t want to stop everything.

But I don’t seem to enjoy them the way I did. I’m there, but it’s like I’m behind a pane of glass. And even my garden, or cooking something for the neighbors—those used to give me a little lift, and lately they just… don’t, really. Is that what you’re asking?
Have your symptoms lasted for more than two months?
No, not more than two months… it’s been about a month, really, since my sister died so suddenly. I hope I’m answering that clearly.
Have you noticed any improvement in how you've been feeling since these thoughts and feelings started about a month ago?

Not a big improvement, no… I mean, I’ve had a few slightly easier moments, I suppose. But overall it’s still been going on since my sister died so unexpectedly, about a month ago. I hope that answers what you mean.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but now find you have no pleasure in at all?

Well… I wouldn’t want to say I have no pleasure in anything at all. I still do make myself go to book club, and sometimes the dance night, because I know it’s probably good for me.

But it feels different lately. I’m sort of sitting there like I’m behind a pane of glass, not really part of it. And even things like my garden, or cooking something for the neighbors… they used to give me a little lift, and now they just don’t seem to. Does that make sense?

I think I may have said this a little already, but… yes, in a way. I still make myself go to book club or the dance night, so it’s not as if I’ve completely stopped doing things. But lately I feel sort of separate when I’m there, like I’m behind a pane of glass.

Yes, I think so. It’s been about a month now… since my sister died so unexpectedly. So, less than three months, yes.

I don’t know that it’s been a significant amount exactly… I haven’t really been keeping track. But food just doesn’t call to me much anymore. I’ll make a little toast or some soup, and then by evening I realize I’ve barely eaten. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything, it just sort of happens.
